exceptions.deactivationNote: Wave 3 closed 2026-08-03. Next wave should isolate per build group, not per package.

releaseGates.name: Commercial
exitCriteria: A new version of studio/contracts/commercial-terms.*.json supersedes v1 and encodes exactly the ratified position: EUR 1,500 standard and EUR 1,000 founding, both inclusive of VAT at the prevailing rate (D-021), foundingCohortSize 25, coupleAccessMonths 18 with the D-022 grace rule represented, and no numeric activation allowance. Its unresolved array no longer contains venue_activation_allowance or venue_calendar_month_semantics. Evidence: the file, a diff against v1, and pnpm test green in studio. (E02.01, E02.06, E02.12)

node scripts/check-venue-edition-contract.mjs has been re-pointed at the ratified figures and exits 0, and its assertions on src/app/layout.tsx publish the two-rate offer rather than one exact price. The gate fails while the enforcement script still asserts the 2026-07-11 position. Evidence: the diff and the passing output. (E02.01, I-002)

Each of E02.01 through E02.12 has a written ratification record naming the position taken, the D-number it derives from, and the position it supersedes, or an explicit statement that there was nothing to supersede. Evidence: a twelve-row table with no empty cell. (E02.01 to E02.12)

The superseded HQ decision is actually superseded in the repository: studio/content/hq/decisions/venue-edition-fixed-price-2026-07-11.md carries a superseded status naming its replacement, and a new dated HQ decision records the Founding 25 position. Evidence: both paths plus node scripts/check-content-truth.mjs passing. I-002 closes with a stated basis, not by lapse. (E02.01, D-009)

A committed string-sweep script, run over a named file list, returns zero hits for the retired commercial position on any surface a venue can reach: no standalone EUR 1,500 without the founding rate, no 'first fifteen', no '40/80', no 'allotment' in venue-facing copy, and zero occurrences of 'for life', 'forever', 'lifetime' or 'guaranteed'. Machine fields scoped out deliberately, never by disabling the sweep when it first trips. Evidence: the script, its output, and the file list. (E02.02, E02.03, E07.07, R-008, R-020)

The published price-reduction wording is the single ratified sentence from D-009 point 2 and nothing else. The sweep confirms 'one-third', '33.3%' and '33%' appear on no venue-facing surface. Evidence: the sweep output and the surface list it covered. (E02.02)

Continuity is a decision table with no blank cells. For each of missed payment, cancellation, lapse, later reactivation, venue sale, company acquisition, operator change, rebrand, merger, relocation, and an additional property brought by a new owner, the table states whether the EUR 1,000 rate survives, what happens to already-redeemed couple workspaces under the D-020 survival rule, and the notice period. 'To be decided' in any row fails the gate. Evidence: the table and the matching clause in the E03.03 draft. (E02.04, E02.05)

Founding-place mechanics are a state machine with a named trigger per transition: available, held for 14 days from proposal once and extendable by Ethan personally, expired, signed, paid at which point number 01/25 to 25/25 is assigned, and programme closed at 25. The record names which system holds the authoritative counter, who can change it, and what happens if two venues pay for place 25 within the same hour. Evidence: the state-machine document and the counter's location per E15.16. (E02.10, E02.11, D-009 points 6 and 7)

The Founding Venue Benefits Charter is published and every benefit carries its boundary on the same line: one 30-minute founder call per venue per year, the named email route, what early access and priority support mean in hours or releases, and the explicit statement that founding requests shape the roadmap and nothing is built for one venue. No benefit is stated without a limit. Evidence: the charter plus a reviewer checklist confirming a limit against every benefit line. (E02.08, E02.09, D-008 scope addition, D-014 point 2)

The unit-economics model is rebuilt at both VAT positions and both are recorded: EUR 1,000 gross and EUR 813.01 net at 23 percent, each with break-even couples per year in the base and heavy usage profiles, plus a one-sentence statement of what changes if Revenue answers yes to accountable-person status. It reconciles into studio/content/hq/finance/ rather than standing alone. Evidence: the finance pack diff, the break-even figures, and agreement with evidence/E02.12-entitlement-choice.md. (E02.12, R-021, R-022, R-018)

No venue-facing document, order form, proposal, FAQ, email or page contains a seat count, allotment, cap, or a numeric pause presented alongside 'unlimited'. The internal fair-use ceiling appears only in internal operating documents. Evidence: the string sweep extended to entitlement vocabulary plus a named reviewer's per-document verdict. (D-020 point 1, E02.12, E07.07)

The offer freeze is real and dated. On 2026-08-15 the ratified commercial position is tagged in version control and every subsequent change to price, terms, entitlement or founding mechanics carries a CR number. The pass note records that the founder read the whole offer in one sitting from a single page and saw both accepted exposures in figures: roughly EUR 750 a year lost on a flagship venue under R-021, and roughly EUR 4,675 a year absorbed under R-022. Evidence: the tag or commit, the CHANGELOG entry, the one-page offer sheet, and the pass basis in the founder's own words. (E01.11, D-008 point 3, PROJECT.md section 20)

Every freeze date ratified in D-008 was either observed on its date or moved by a numbered change request. No freeze passed silently. For each of offer 2026-08-15, UI 2026-08-20, copy 2026-08-21, capture 2026-08-22, film lock 2026-08-28 and release candidate 2026-08-30, the record states which of the two happened and names the evidence: the tag or commit that froze it, or the CR number that moved it. Evidence: the six-row table plus project-control.mjs freeze output. (E01.11, D-008 clause 3, D-025)

releaseGates.name: Legal
exitCriteria: All six documents drafted, each recording on its face the named, dated, publicly available Irish or EU source position it was built from, or recording explicitly that it is bespoke.

A written GDPR role map exists and is founder-ratified (E03.01), covering every data category including Article 9 categories and children data, with controller/processor/joint-controller position and lawful basis for each.

Each document passed adversarial review by the lane that did not draft it, across four lenses (GDPR completeness, consumer contract fairness, commercial enforceability, hostile reading), each completing a per-item checklist with an explicit verdict per item.
Every finding disposed of in writing: fixed, or accepted by the founder with his stated reason. Nothing flagged and silently shipped.
No statutory reference, case citation or legal proposition appears in any published document unless verified against primary source text, with source and retrieval date in a citation register.

A written VAT and revenue-recognition position exists, sourced to current Revenue guidance, answering in order: accountable-person status by receipt of foreign B2B services, the tax point on annual prepayment, threshold aggregation, and OSS. The Revenue MyEnquiries reply is attached as evidence. Every agreement states the price as INCLUSIVE of VAT at the prevailing rate (D-021).

The contracting entity is correct and stated on every agreement (registered name and CRO number), or the founder has decided in writing to contract personally with the personal-liability exposure recorded as accepted.

GDPR operational paperwork current: Article 30 record, subprocessor register with each vendor DPA on file, documented transfer basis per non-EEA processor, and a written Article 35 DPIA threshold assessment reaching a reasoned conclusion either way.

An automated string check plus founder review confirms no published document, page, portal string, email, film line or proposal states or implies legal approval, solicitor review, accountant verification, or unqualified GDPR compliance. Pre-approved answers exist for the four questions venues ask.
A signed founder statement names what has NOT been done: no solicitor, no accountant, no professional indemnity, no privilege over review records. R-013 and R-014 open and accepted.
The gate pass is recorded as founder-accepted without professional review, with the date and the founder own words. Never as legal review obtained or legally approved in any generated report.

Conditional: if the role map produces joint controllership on venue adoption analytics, an Article 26 arrangement and its public essence summary exist, or the founder has recorded a product decision that removes the trigger.
blockers: CR-001 approved 2026-08-03 under the founder standing instruction (D-023). Reversible on request.

releaseGates.name: Product
exitCriteria: The ratified couple access term is enforced by code end to end. studio/src/lib/entitlements-db/codes.ts accepts a computed duration and refuses anything shorter than 548 days rather than throwing on any value other than 548; the wedding date is stored on the sponsored entitlement at redemption; expiry is max(redemption + 548 days, wedding date + 90 days); and a wedding-date change recomputes expiry later, never earlier. Evidence: a named test covering all four behaviours plus the specific R-015 case, books March 2027, marries September 2028, redeems on signature. The gate fails while the mint guard is a hard equality on VENUE_EDITION_COUPLE_ACCESS_DAYS. (D-022, R-015, E04.07, E04.09, E04.12)

Unlimited entitlement is representable in all four places R-016 names: the mint path accepts an unlimited sponsor without the null-allotment throw; availableCount and the 'No remaining allotment headroom' attention item are suppressed for unlimited sponsors; the HQ near-allotment list excludes them; and studio/src/app/hq/entitlements/OnboardVenueForm.tsx no longer defaults the field to 10. Evidence: the four diffs plus a test asserting a portal payload for an unlimited sponsor contains no seat count, no remaining count and no headroom warning anywhere, including CSV export, PDF, tooltips, support view-as and accessibility text. (D-020, R-016, E07.03, E07.07, E07.08, E07.09)

Article 9 capture has a decided, implemented position. Either dietary and accessibility data is captured at a guest-facing RSVP step where the guest supplies their own data, or it stays couple-entered with all five R-017 controls shipped: structured fields not free text, hard exclusion from any public Timeline payload enforced by a test rather than a clause, retention tied to the wedding date, Article 9 named in the E03.01 role map with the condition relied on, and an under-16 rule. app/src/lib/templates.generated.ts and app/src/app/the-wedding/page.tsx both match the chosen position. Evidence: the code path, the exclusion test, the role-map entry, the two diffs. (R-017, E04.08, E05.03, E06.01)

The privacy boundary is a test, not a promise. One named test asserts that for a fully populated sponsored workspace the venue-visible payload contains no task title, note body, milestone story, photograph, collaborator name, guest name or free-text field, and that the same holds for the CSV export, the PDF report, the support view-as path and any email digest. Evidence: the test file and its output listing the surfaces covered. R-007 cannot be closed by copy review. (E04.08, E07.12, E07.18)

D-011's three ratified product rules are each enforced by a test: a wedding date appears in the portal only where that venue's code was redeemed; a wedding-date change never surfaces as a portal event; and suppression holds at 3 eligible sponsored workspaces for behavioural counts and 5 for percentage cohorts, with the suppressed number absent from tooltips, exports, view-as and accessibility text. Evidence: three named tests. (D-011, E04.09, E07.12)

Every lifecycle state in the E04.07 state machine has a deterministic fixture and a test, including unlink, couple separation, venue non-renewal with redeemed workspaces still live, release-on-cancellation with venue branding and name removed within 24 hours, postponement, expiry into Keepsake, and deletion. Evidence: the fixture manifest plus a test run showing one fixture per documented state with no state unrepresented. (E04.06, E04.07, E04.11, E04.12, D-020 points 2 and 3)

The Keepsake export exists as a produced artifact, not a plan. An export has been generated from a fixture workspace, opened by a human without Signal Studio present, and a test asserts it contains every published milestone plus every private item the couple owns. Evidence: the artifact's format and size, a screenshot of it open, and the test. D-010 point 3 makes the export the thing that keeps the Keepsake promise honest; a promise of an export is not an export. (E03.09, E06.11)

The three sharing modes survive adversarial test: a private link is unguessable with its entropy stated and revocation effective immediately; a password-protected artifact refuses without the password on every route including OG-image and metadata endpoints; and an unpublished artifact returns 404 from a previously cached link. Evidence: app/src/server/share-revocation-contract.test.mjs extended to the sponsored Timeline, named and passing. (E06.05, E06.12)

The design-system review is recorded as artifacts: pnpm ds:check clean in both app and studio, visual-regression baselines committed for every surface appearing in either film, and founder evidence captured at all four breakpoints through studio/scripts/experience/founder-evidence.mjs with its hashes intact. Evidence: the baseline directory, the check outputs, the evidence manifest. (E05.11, E05.12, E06.12, E07.18)

The audit D-015 Q2 mandated is legible. For each task in E04 through E07 the record states whether existing repository work fully satisfies, partially satisfies, or does not satisfy its written acceptance criteria, naming the file paths inspected. A-004 closes with a number rather than staying open. Evidence: the audit table, one row per task, with a total. (D-015 Q2, A-004)

The Account and the Portal are demonstrably one surface. A single authenticated session reaches invitation administration, adoption evidence, account standing, renewal date and support history without a second login or a second product; /hq/venue-portal-review still redirects to /hq/account-review; and no venue-facing string names two products. Evidence: ordered screenshots or a recording covering all five, plus the redirect test. (D-015 Q4, E07.01, E07.16)

End-to-end reconciliation passes on live data, not fixtures. For one venue account in the production-like environment, invitation count, redemption count, activation count and every figure in the generated PDF and CSV agree with the database, carry the same data-through date, and name the metric dictionary version. A single mismatch fails the gate rather than raising needs_attention. Evidence: the reconciliation run showing both sides. (E07.14, E07.15, E07.18, E09.09)

releaseGates.name: Data, security and reliability
exitCriteria: Cross-tenant isolation is proven by tests that try and fail. Named tests attempt to read and to write another venue's sponsors, codes, redemptions, rollups and reports, and to read a couple workspace from a venue session, each asserting refusal at the data layer rather than only at the route. Evidence: app/src/server/cross-tenant-isolation.test.mjs and tenant-scope.test.mjs extended with the sponsored-venue cases, named and passing. (E08.04, E08.05)

Every venue-facing and couple-facing route is enumerated in a committed manifest with its required role, and a test fails when a route exists without an entry. Anonymous, wrong-venue, wrong-role and revoked-member requests are each asserted refused. Evidence: app/scripts/check-route-manifest.mjs extended plus the authorisation-matrix test output. (E08.05, E07.18)

Invitation tokens survive five named attacks, one test each: guessing with entropy stated in bits and redemption rate-limited per address and per account with the enumeration arithmetic shown, reuse after redemption, forwarding to a different account, replay of a captured redemption request, and two concurrent redemptions of the same code. Evidence: five named tests, all passing. (E08.06)

A restore actually happened. pnpm recovery:drill is run against a real backup of every production database carrying venue or couple data; the restored copy is queried to confirm a known sponsored workspace and its redemptions are present; and wall-clock time from decision to restored is recorded. RPO and RTO are recorded as measured numbers, not targets. Evidence: the drill output with timestamps and the restored-row proof. A backup that has never been restored is not a backup. (E08.09)

The incident runbook names a person, a channel and a clock for each of: breach affecting couple data, breach affecting venue data, total outage, silent data corruption, and a wrongly issued or wrongly expired entitlement. It records the 72-hour GDPR Article 33 notification clock and where the DPC is contacted. It has been walked through once as a tabletop, and the absence of paid on-call is recorded as an accepted limitation of the zero budget. Evidence: the runbook and the tabletop record. (E08.08, E08.12, D-015 Q5)

Billing is tested with real money once, before any venue is invoiced. One founding agreement at EUR 1,000 is charged and refunded in production; the immutable founding-rate flag and historical price record are written and cannot be edited from the operator UI; the invoice states the price as inclusive of VAT at the prevailing rate; and the payment is individually identifiable so treatment can be corrected retrospectively. Evidence: the transaction ID, the refund ID, the invoice PDF showing the VAT wording, and the immutability test. (E08.01, E08.02, E15.02, D-021, R-018)

Renewal, failed payment, grace and lapse each fire against a clock in test: renewal invoice, reminder, failed-payment retry schedule, grace-period end, and lapse, with the D-020 survival rule asserted, that a lapsed venue's already-redeemed workspaces keep full term plus Keepsake and only new issuance stops. Evidence: a time-travel test covering all five transitions plus the survival assertion. (E08.03, D-020 point 2)

Upload handling is honest about what a zero budget buys: file type validated by content rather than extension, size limits enforced server-side, private storage with signed time-limited URLs, no user-supplied file served from an origin that can execute it, and EXIF stripped from milestone photographs. The absence of commercial malware scanning is recorded as an accepted residual with the founder's note. Evidence: the tests, the storage configuration, and the recorded residual. (E08.07)

Performance budgets are measured on the surfaces that carry the product's claim: the shared Timeline on a mid-range mobile over a throttled connection, the portal Overview, and the couple briefing. pnpm budgets:check and pnpm performance:measure produce recorded numbers against stated budgets and a regression fails the build. Evidence: the budget file, the measured run, the CI wiring. (E08.10)

Instrumentation reconciles across three layers at least once. A scripted run creates an invitation, redeems it, performs a first meaningful action, publishes a Timeline and enters Keepsake; each of those five transitions is asserted present in the event stream, in the daily rollup and in the venue's report, with counts matching at every layer, duplicate source events proven idempotent, and every number in the report carrying its metric dictionary version, denominator, reporting window and coverage state. Evidence: the script and its three-layer output. (E09.01, E09.02, E09.03, E09.09, E07.15)

The demonstration fixture is deterministic and its imagery's provenance is recorded. The one-action demo reset restores the canonical Glenmara House and Mara-and-Finn state identically across all four products and the portal on two consecutive runs; every demonstration image records how it was generated (model, prompt or source, date), because D-012 replaced licensing with generation and there is no licence to file; and a named reviewer confirms no unapproved real venue or couple material appears. Evidence: the reset diffed twice, the image provenance register, the reviewer verdict. (E09.06, E09.07, E09.08, E09.12, D-012, A-007, R-011)

Release engineering is executed, not documented. The three steps in studio/content/hq/operator-todos/open-signal-studio-2026-09-01.md are individually completed and ticked: the redeploy that flips the statically generated surfaces, the marketing-CTA decision, and the /app allowlist decision. Every venue-reachable URL is re-fetched after the deploy and confirmed to show post-launch state, and the rollback procedure has been executed once against a staging deploy. Evidence: the closed operator-todo, the post-deploy fetch of each URL, and the rollback run output. (E08.12, D-007, DEP-005)

releaseGates.name: Creative
exitCriteria: Every deliverable render has a manifest that validates against signal-motion/src/render/manifest-schema.ts, and each manifest's output.sha256 matches the file on disk when re-hashed by the Claude lane. Evidence: the manifest paths and the Claude-lane re-hash output. A render without a passing manifest is not a deliverable. (E13.17, E14.17)

No deliverable was rendered from a dirty tree. Every manifest records code.dirty false and a code.gitSha that resolves to a commit on a pushed branch. Evidence: git cat-file -e per manifest, run by the Claude lane. This is the single criterion that makes every other creative criterion reproducible. (E13.17, E14.18)

corepack pnpm verify passes in signal-motion at the exact commit the deliverables were rendered from: typecheck, tests, check:deps, check:ds, check:assets, check:copy-fit, check:compositions, check:motion, check:docs, and remotion compositions. Evidence: the full command output with the SHA, run by the Claude lane at that SHA rather than pasted from the motion lane.

A licence register in signal-motion/docs/ gives, per audio and font asset, the source URL, the licence name, the retrieval date, and the specific permission for commercial use in an email to businesses. Every distinct assets[].sha256 in the deliverable manifests appears in the register. The register must cover the music and sound bed even though scripts/write-render-manifest.mts currently populates assets[] from FONT_ASSETS only, so the manifests alone cannot close R-012. Evidence: the register, the hash cross-check, and the diff extending the manifest writer to audio. (E13.13, E14.16, R-012)

The Cohort 1 deliverables are 25 distinct files, each named to the project fixture composition profile convention, each with a distinct output.sha256, and each tied by manifest input.sha256 to the specific venue record it was rendered for. Evidence: 25 paths, 25 distinct hashes, and the venue-to-render mapping. Two identical hashes means two venues received the same film. (E13.15, E13.17)

Each of the 25 renders is checked frame-accurately for the two things that break a personalised film. The Claude lane extracts a still at the recipient-highlight frame for all 25, contact-sheets them, and records per render that the correct venue name is shown and that no other venue's name is legible, per the E13.05 anonymity rule and E10.14 consent status. Evidence: the contact sheet and a 25-row verdict list. (E13.05, E13.06, E13.17, E10.14)

Every word of on-screen and spoken copy in both films exists as text in the repository, and the same automated string check used by the legal gate runs over those files with zero hits for 'forever', 'for life', 'lifetime', 'guaranteed', 'GDPR compliant', 'legally approved', 'solicitor' or 'reviewed by'. Copy that exists only inside a composition's JSX cannot be checked and fails this criterion. Evidence: the copy files and the check output. (D-016, R-008, E13.07, E13.09, E14.12)

Before the Day contains no price. A stills sweep of the full master at a stated frame interval, plus the on-screen copy file, confirms no euro sign, no '1,500', no '1,000' and no price wording anywhere in the film. Evidence: the sweep output and the copy file. D-014 ratified this and the film is the easiest place to lose it. (D-014, E14.13)

Product-accuracy QA is a comparison, not an assertion. exitCriteria: Cohort 1 is 25 named venues in the CRM, each carrying a verified buyer contact with a verification date within 30 days of the send, a verified email address, coordinates that plot inside the 45-minute drive-time ring, eligibility confirmed against D-012's in and out venue-type lists, and one written venue-specific reason it belongs. Evidence: the CRM completeness export by field, held in Signal HQ and never in the project tree. Any blank verification date means the cohort is not locked. (E10.06, E10.07, E10.08, E10.11, E10.12, R-005)

The researched universe is at least 125 accounts, or the shortfall is formally documented with the number actually found and what was searched. Deduplication is complete across venue groups, multi-property hotels, shared operators and renamed properties, with the number of merged rows recorded. Evidence: the universe count and the dedup log. This is the criterion that says out loud whether 25 signed venues is arithmetically available. (E10.04, E10.05)

Deliverability is proven before the first real send, not assumed. SPF, DKIM and DMARC pass on signalstudio.ie as shown by raw headers on a real received message rather than by a DNS record existing; the domain's sending history is stated; and an inbox-placement test to a seed set across Gmail, Outlook and one Irish ISP records where each message landed. Evidence: the raw headers, the seed results, the dates. (E11.04, R-010)

Sending mechanics match D-013 exactly and are verifiable from the sent message rather than the configuration screen: film link-click tracking on, open tracking off with no tracking pixel present in the HTML, a one-click unsubscribe header, and a suppression list honoured by the sending path. Evidence: the raw source of a real test send showing no pixel and the unsubscribe header, plus a test that a suppressed address is refused. (D-013 point 3, E11.04, E03.11)

The complete sequence has been rehearsed once, end to end, against a rehearsal account before any real venue is touched: introduction email sent and received, film link clicked, meeting booked through the booking flow, discovery structure used, walkthrough delivered, proposal and order form issued, 14-day hold started, and the account moved through every CRM stage including 'later' after the fourth touch. Evidence: the rehearsal account's full stage history, the artifacts produced at each step, and a written list of what broke. A sequence never walked is a document, not a system. (E11.02, E11.05, E11.08 to E11.11, E11.13, E11.14, D-013 point 4)

The venue marketing-controls package exists and is attached to the agreement, not only to the pack: the approved copy pack, a one-page prohibited-claims sheet naming 'forever', 'guaranteed', permanence or storage promises, 'GDPR compliant' and any claim that legal review was obtained, and the clause in the master agreement requiring correction within a stated period. Evidence: the copy pack, the sheet, and the clause reference in the E03.02 draft. R-020 is the only risk on the register that reaches outside Signal Studio's own strings. (R-020, E03.02, E12.12)

Every commercial surface a Cohort 1 venue can reach is enumerated as a list and QA'd per dimension: the public landing page, the private Founding 25 invitation page, the parameterised proposal page, the film landing destination, the certificate, the sales kit, the deck and the one-page proposal. Each has a recorded verdict on copy, price presentation, privacy explanation, responsive, accessibility and performance. Evidence: the surface list with a verdict per dimension per surface. A surface not on the list is a surface nobody checked. (E12.01 to E12.14)

The price is presented identically wherever a venue can see it: EUR 1,500 standard, EUR 1,000 founding, both inclusive of VAT at the prevailing rate, annual prepaid, with the founding conditions attached, including the schema.org offer markup in studio/src/app/layout.tsx. Evidence: a per-surface string sweep confirming no surface states a price without the VAT wording and the conditions. (E12.04, D-009, D-021)

The personalised delivery path works end to end for one venue before it runs for 25: a tracked link is generated, resolves to that venue's landing destination, plays the film without a large attachment, records the click, and the click appears in the founder operating dashboard. Evidence: the test link, the recorded click, the dashboard row. (E11.07, E13.16, E09.04, E09.05)

The objection library answers the questions this specific offer creates, with a written answer per question matching the ratified position rather than improvising a new one: why EUR 1,000 and not EUR 1,500; what the price lock does on a venue sale; what unlimited means and what happens at fair use; what the venue sees and never sees; whether a solicitor reviewed the contract, using the pre-approved answer from the legal gate; what happens to couples if Signal Studio stops; and why there is no in-person meeting. Evidence: the library plus a cross-check of each answer against its D-number. (E11.12, E12.08, D-016, D-018)

Consent is tracked per venue before any name is published. The E10.14 consent field is populated for every Cohort 1 account, and the map, the site and the certificate publish only where consent is recorded. Evidence: the consent field state per account and a check that the published surfaces name only consented venues. (E10.14, E15.16, PROJECT.md section 21)

No contact data has leaked into the project tree or a generated report. project-control.mjs validate passes, private/venues.csv is confirmed gitignored and untracked via git ls-files, and a scan of PROJECT_STATE.json, STATUS.md, BACKLOG.md and evidence/ finds no email address, phone number, postal address or venue name presented as a participant. Evidence: the scan output and the git ls-files result. (PROJECT.md section 21, REPORTING.md section 5)

A written list records what broke and what was changed as a result. Evidence: the rehearsal account's configuration record, the redeemed invitation, a screenshot of the venue-side evidence, and the what-broke list. Nothing certifies that what was sold can be delivered until one venue has actually been onboarded by the person who will onboard the other twenty-four. (E15.09, E15.10, E15.11, R-024, D-025)

tasks.title: Complete invitation creation, copying, sending, resending, revoking, replacing, expiring and redemption status.
tasks.dependencyBasis: D-020 point 1: the fair-use ceiling that notifies rather than blocks lives in invitation creation.
acceptanceCriteria: A venue can CREATE an invitation from the portal surface and COPY its code/link; creation persists and the new invitation appears in the list.
SEND and RESEND exist as actions; each writes a real timestamp to the activation lifecycle record, and the surface distinguishes not-sent from sent.
REVOKE and REPLACE exist; revoke makes the code unredeemable, replace issues a fresh code against the same activation with the old one dead.
EXPIRE is represented from a stored expiry column, never defaulted or computed when the column is null; an expired invitation cannot be redeemed and reads as expired.
REDEMPTION STATUS shows the full ladder (not sent / sent / accepted / declined / expired / revoked) from real data, degrading to unknown rather than to a wrong state when columns are unbackfilled.
The fair-use ceiling notifies HQ and never blocks creation (D-020 pt 1). No venue-facing numeric refusal on create.
Every mutation is authorised to the acting sponsor's own scope, and no invitation payload carries notes/task/project/briefing/comment/attachment/collaborator or private Timeline content.
The live loader selects deliveredAt and expiresAt so the code-state ladder can reach 'issued' and 'expired'.
A single substrate decision is made and recorded: which table carries the invitation, which carries redemption truth, and which wins when they disagree.
sponsor_activations is wired for the first time and joined to the code ledger.
Create, copy, send, resend, revoke and expire exist as server actions with per-sponsor authorisation.
Replace is a single operation that withdraws the old invitation and issues its replacement.
Every mutation writes an auditable row.
Each action fails closed without a named operator, the way lib/hq/operator-identity.ts intends.
Destructive actions carry type-to-confirm friction enforced server-side, as hq/entitlements/actions.ts:163 does.
A redemption on license_codes moves an invitation to accepted.
deliveredAt and expiresAt are actually selected so states stop degrading.
Every new payload goes through assertSnapshotPrivacy.
No message leaves the system; 'send' means marking an invitation issued and producing wording for a human.

evidence.note: The entire server-action surface: one loader, one request-recorder. No create/send/resend/revoke/replace/expire.
SPONSOR_INVITATION_STATES and the invitation/activation timestamp columns already model the full lifecycle the task asks for.

deliveredAt/expiresAt are not selected, so sent/expired states degrade on live data.
assertSnapshotPrivacy has exactly one call site — new invitation payload paths would be unchecked by default.
recordMoreAccessRequestAction accepts a caller-supplied sponsorId with no per-sponsor authorisation check — the pattern any new mutation must not copy.

tasks.title: Complete Account, organisation settings, members, roles, support history and reporting preferences.
acceptanceCriteria: A venue user can authenticate as themselves: a venue-scoped identity exists and the account surface is reachable by it, not by a single shared operator secret.
The members list on the live path returns the real administrators of that venue from a persisted store, and is non-empty for a venue with at least one admin.
Invite member performs a persisted server-side mutation that survives a reload, not a client-side notice string.
roles.ts governs the live path: a capability is checked server-side against the authenticated venue user's role before a mutating action runs, and a role lacking it is refused.
Organisation settings are persisted per venue and tenant-scoped so venue A cannot read or write venue B, and branding stays venue-name-only per D-027 point 3.
Support history is that venue's real record from a data source, or is explicitly presented as unavailable; never a hardcoded array presented as fact.
Reporting preferences persist per venue and their payload carries no couple-private content and no per-person ranking.
AC-2 Organisation identity shows venue name, edition, term start and end, renewal date and standing, all read from `sponsors`, none hard-coded.
AC-3 Venue branding on every Account surface is the venue's name only — no logo, no venue-written message, no free-text field (D-027 point 3).
AC-4 Members and roles are either live and audited, or absent by decision with the surface stating Signal Studio administers the account. A role selector that governs nothing satisfies neither.
AC-5 The capability matrix in docs/venue-portal/ROLES_AND_PERMISSIONS.md and the shipped list in lib/account/roles.ts agree, or the divergence is recorded as a dated decision.
AC-6 Support and request history is either real sponsor_requests rows or an explicit nothing-recorded state; illustrative rows never render on live data.
AC-7 Reporting preferences are persisted and honoured, or the control is absent.
AC-8 No Account payload, export or page contains private content or a plaintext licence code, proved by a test over the payload.
AC-9 Every mutation reachable from the Account writes an audit event naming a real actor; attribution to 'whoever held the credential' fails.
Conflicts that no ratified decision settles are recorded, not silently reconciled (WORKFLOWS §8).
AC-1 A named principal can reach the Account surface for exactly one venue, resolved server-side from the session and never from a client-supplied identifier.

evidence.note: One shared password derives one token for all operators; no per-venue credential exists.
The sole route guard checks only the shared token, then redirects to /hq/access.
members: [] is returned unconditionally on every live snapshot.

loadLiveVenueSnapshotAction accepts any slug with no per-venue authorisation; recordMoreAccessRequestAction runs no capability check.

acceptanceCriteria: A venue's annual charge is derivable in code from one place: plan (founding|paid) to amount in cents, matching contracts/commercial-terms.v2.json (100000 / 150000), with a test that fails if the two drift.
Every venue-facing money string renders VAT-inclusive with the exact D-021 wording 'inclusive of VAT at the prevailing rate', never VAT-added and never a separate VAT line implying it is on top.
A prepaid annual term records termStartsAt, termEndsAt, paidAt and the amount actually received, and is individually identifiable for retrospective VAT correction (R-014, R-022).
The recording path refuses the standard price against a founding plan and the reverse, proven by test.
There is exactly one live writer that records a cleared payment, and it carries every guard. A second unguarded path does not exist.

The payment capture route is stated honestly: either a built path exists end to end, or the documented answer is that venues are invoiced out of band and recorded by CLI, with no surface claiming otherwise.

D-022's couple-term rule is not reimplemented here; billing links to venue-lifecycle.ts as the single source.
Money is constructed from gross only: net is always derived, never an input, and net + VAT reconciles to gross exactly for every amount and rate.

evidence.note: vatInclusive() is the only constructor and takes gross. net = round(gross*10000/(10000+rate)), vat = gross - net, so net+vat===gross by construction. No constructor accepts a net amount. Null rate means 'not determined', never zero-rated.

tasks.title: Complete role-based authentication and authorisation across venue owners, managers, viewers and couples.
acceptanceCriteria: The role set is enumerated in one place per surface — venue roles in studio, workspace roles in the app — with no third undocumented set, and any divergence between documentation and code is stated explicitly rather than reconciled silently.
Every role check runs server-side; no capability is enforced only by hiding a control in the UI.
Every cell of the venue capability matrix is asserted against the shipped module, not against the test's own copy, and a capability added to the module without a recorded decision fails the build.
No venue role may hold a capability naming couple content or couple identity, proven by a mutation that adds one and turns the suite red.
The venue-facing read path cannot reach the app database, and the venue projector cannot fetch anything at all.

The Signal HQ session token is not derivable from the password, carries a server-side expiry, cannot be forged by editing its issue time, and does not survive password rotation — each proven by a test written to fail against the previous implementation.
Every /hq surface is gated or waived in writing, and the session token is minted in exactly one place.
Whatever is not implemented by 1 September is stated as not implemented, with the interim operating model named (D-016, R-043).
The evidence cites the guard by file for each role check, not a description of one.

evidence.note: FIXED. AccountCapability was a bare union type, which cannot be enumerated at runtime — the root cause of the guard failure below. Now ACCOUNT_CAPABILITIES is a runtime `as const` array with the type derived from it, plus ACCOUNT_ROLES derived from ROLE_CAPABILITIES' keys (which TypeScript already forces to be exhaustive).

FIXED on two counts. (1) It was NEVER WIRED INTO `pnpm test` — it had not run in CI once, while roles.ts cited it in its own header as the enforcement. (2) It iterated its own hand-written copy of the capability list, so it could not see a new capability at all. Now reads ACCOUNT_CAPABILITIES/ACCOUNT_ROLES from the shipped module and adds a suite asserting the recorded matrix matches the module in both directions.
role-matrix.test.ts wired into the studio test script. Confirmed it now executes in the full run.

AUDITED AND KEPT unchanged — the predecessor's v2 rewrite is correct. v1 cookie was sha256('signal-hq-session:v1:'+password): derivable offline, an offline oracle for the password itself, and no server-side expiry. v2 is `v2.<issuedAt>.<HMAC>` over a PBKDF2-150k-derived key. Its header states plainly that this is still a shared password and that a venue must never be given it.
AUDITED AND KEPT. Twelve malformed-input cases fail closed; each property test is written to fail against v1 and does. Wired into CI by the checkpoint.

AUDITED AND KEPT, 5 tests passing. Pins that proxy.ts verifies rather than recomputing, that every /hq page and route handler is gated or waived in writing, that only auth.ts may mint a token, that no venue-facing module may reach TASKS_DATABASE_URL, and that the venue projector cannot fetch.

Section 3 carries the full role and permission matrix: venue owner/manager/viewer with the enforcing file per capability, plus couple, collaborator, guest (a token, not a role), venue (no identity exists) and HQ operator. Also records the unreconciled four-role-doc vs three-role-code disagreement.
Task specification written to the TASK.md template.

DEFECT I FOUND. Line 60: `const [role, setRole] = useState<AccountRole>("owner")`. The role is client state chosen from a picker. There is no server-side notion of which role a caller holds anywhere in the product, so no venue role check can run server-side by construction.

tasks.title: Secure invitation tokens against guessing, reuse, unintended forwarding, replay and duplicate redemption.
acceptanceCriteria: A newly minted couple invitation code carries at least 48 bits of entropy, with the arithmetic computed in a test rather than asserted in prose, and the test fails if the length or alphabet is reduced.
Exactly one invitation-code generator exists per repository; a source-contract test fails if a local re-implementation reappears.

Code characters are drawn uniformly. The test proving it carries a control that runs the previous biased draw and must fail the same bound, so a bound too loose to detect the defect cannot pass as a green test.

share_links stores sha256 under a UNIQUE index and never the secret; proven by dumping the whole table after a mint and asserting the secret is absent, against a database built from the checked-in migration 0027 SQL.
Neither the stored hash nor the public row id opens a share link; both are proven to resolve to null.
Every share link minted before migration 0027 still resolves, and a backfilled row cannot be opened by its public id through the legacy branch.
Share-link resolution never crosses a tenant boundary and never revives an archived workspace, proven on both branches of the dual-read resolver.
The redemption path consults its attempt budget before it looks the code up, proven by a source-contract test on statement order, so no unmetered 'does this code exist' oracle exists.
Every test above runs in pnpm test. A security test that is not registered is not a control.
The limiter's failure mode (open, and unenforced until Upstash is provisioned) is stated in the source file, not only in a document.

evidence.note: Full criterion-to-proof trace, the audit of the interrupted checkpoint, the two-live-redemption-writers finding, and the real command output including the two failures seen and how they were attributed.

The single studio generator. 31-symbol alphabet, 10-character body = 31^10 ≈ 2^49.5, drawn with crypto randomInt (unbiased). Replaces generateCode(prefix,5) in scripts/issue-codes.ts (31^5 ≈ 2^24.8) and genLicenseCode() in hq/entitlements/actions.ts (31^8 ≈ 2^39.6).

The app-side generator, extracted out of the 'use server' comp.ts so a test can load it. Replaces newCode(), which was 7 hex chars off a UUID = 2^28 with a Math.random() fallback. Rejection sampling; throws rather than falling back when no CSPRNG exists.

13 tests. The uniformity test carries its own control: it runs the old randomBytes%31 draw in the same run and asserts it EXCEEDS the bound the new draw must sit under, so a bound too loose to detect the defect cannot pass as green.

23 tests, all now passing. Before this session it had NEVER RUN: it imported resolveShareLinkRowWith from @/server/db/queries (server-only, and no such export) so it threw on load, and it was not registered in pnpm test.

Rewired to import nothing server-only and take its database as an argument (the Timeline recordQualifiedViewWith pattern). The checkpoint's version imported db from ./index, which pulled server-only back in transitively and defeated its own stated purpose.

redeemCompCodeImpl now resolves identity and spends redeemWithinAttemptLimits BEFORE the comp_codes lookup. The limiter's fail-open behaviour and the unprovisioned Upstash dependency are stated in the file and asserted by a test.

Was RED on main: it asserts the archived-workspace guard inside queries.ts, and the checkpoint moved that guard out. Repointed at the resolver and strengthened to count both branches of the dual read.

The script whose own comments call the Tasks comp_codes row 'runtime redemption' and the studio license_codes row 'sponsor audit'. This is the proof that the guarded path is the audit copy and the unguarded one is what couples reach.

Clean against D-009/D-016/D-020/D-021.

PRODUCTION CALLER CONFIRMED. Line 27 imports resolveShareLinkRowWith; line 715 binds it to the live `db`. Grepped: this is the only non-test caller, so the tested control is the one that runs. This is the failure mode the programme keeps hitting (a control tested but never called) and it does NOT apply here.

It is NOT a comment-only first segment. All three statements run. tasks.title: Secure photograph and attachment uploads with file validation, malware controls, size limits and private storage.
acceptanceCriteria: An upload is refused unless its declared type is on an allowlist; types nobody enumerated are refused by absence, proven for ten types including SVG, HTML, XML and executables.
A file whose bytes disagree with its declared type is refused, proven by the exact bypass the previous denylist had: HTML content declared image/png.
The MIME type written to attachments.mime_type is the validated type, never the raw client string, proven by a source-contract test.
Validation runs before the metadata row is claimed, so a refused file never reaches the database.
Formats with no dependable magic number are marked as unverified rather than reported as checked.

The download route does not redirect to a blob URL. Private blobs are streamed through the route, after the workspace check, proven by a source contract; put and get are proven to agree on access: 'private'.
The security headers (nosniff, sandbox CSP, private no-store) apply to every backend, with exactly one header block so a future branch cannot skip them.
A cross-tenant attachment id still returns 404, never 403.
The production storage backend is reported as it actually is, and the absence of malware scanning is stated with its cost and its trigger.

evidence.note: Criterion-to-proof trace, the four-row audit of what the task title claims against what existed, the malware-scanning cost table with a recommendation, and an explicit list of what the evidence does NOT claim.

The allowlist with byte signatures. Replaces an 8-entry DENYLIST checked against the client-supplied file.type string — two compounded failures: anything not on the list passed, and the label could simply be changed. SVG/HTML/XML/executables are refused by ABSENCE, which is the point.

16 tests. Includes the exact old bypass — HTML content declared image/png — plus MZ-executable-as-PDF, SVG-as-PNG, JPEG-as-PNG and RIFF/AVI-as-WebP (which checks the WebP wildcard bytes have not made every RIFF file a WebP).

chooseBackend() returns 'vercel-no-token' and putBytes THROWS when BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN is absent. New openBlobStream() reads via get(url, {access:'private'}) with the store token, because a private blob URL is not fetchable by a browser.

Response.redirect(url, 302) to a PRIVATE blob is removed. That redirect sent the browser to a URL requiring an Authorization header it does not have; it had never fired only because the store is unprovisioned, so it would have fired on the day the token was added. Security headers now cover both backends from one block.
status: open, priority: P1, blocking: true. This is the proof that BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN is unprovisioned and therefore that attachment upload is broken in production today.

The SDK's own type declarations, lines 128-132 and 202-212: "'private': The blob requires authentication to access" and get()'s note that "The authorization header is automatically set". This is the static proof that the 302 could not have worked.

Not in the submitted evidence list but it is where the change lands. `validateUpload(` at line 181, `.insert(attachments)` at line 214 — C4 verified by reading the file, not only by the offset test. `const mimeType = verdict.mimeType` at line 195 verifies C3. `verdict.sniffed` is never read.

evidence.ref: upload-path completeness check (my own, not the builder's)
evidence.note: I grepped for every byte-writing path: `putBytes`, `arrayBuffer()`, `instanceof File`, `insert(attachments)`, `insert(resources)`. `uploadAttachmentAction` is the ONLY one. `addLinkResourceAction` inserts links, never bytes. So there is no second, unvalidated upload route — the coverage claim is genuine.

tasks.title: Complete audit logging, operational logging, error monitoring and alert escalation.
acceptanceCriteria: The audit log and the operational log are defined in one place in code, naming both audit tables (workspace_events, entitlement_events), and a test fails if that definition is removed.

No server-scope console call may log an email address, a rendered email body, a task or workspace title, guest or dietary data, or a URL that can be a bearer token, proven by a test shown to fire on each of those seven shapes and shown NOT to fire on four ordinary error logs.

A new server-scope logging site cannot be added without a change to a recorded list, proven by a ratchet test whose comparison direction is itself asserted, plus a guard that fails if the scan finds nothing.

The two identified leaks are closed at source: the CSP collector no longer writes /share/<token> to the log, and sendEmail no longer writes the recipient or a body preview outside NODE_ENV development.

On a database built from the checked-in entitlements baseline, UPDATE and DELETE against entitlement_events are refused after apply-audit-ledger-triggers.mjs runs, and demonstrably NOT refused before it runs.
A command reports the absence of append-only enforcement and exits non-zero; the integrity checker treats absence as a failing run rather than a clean one.
No source comment claims an enforcement the schema does not deliver, held by a test that fails if the retired wording returns.
The state of error monitoring and alerting is recorded as fact, including naming what is not provisioned, and no surface implies monitoring exists that does not (D-016).

evidence.note: NEW. The written distinction plus the only sanctioned console sink. opLog takes scalars only, so spreading a database row into a log call does not type-check. Exports redactForLog/redactEmail/safeError, reusing sentry-scrub's redactSensitiveUrl so the console path applies the same rule Sentry already applied.

NEW, 8/8 pass, wired into pnpm test. RULE 1 ratchet over 51 recorded logging sites across 31 files (unrecorded file fails, grown count fails, stale entry fails). RULE 2 denylist proven to fire on document-uri, args.to, args.html, task.title, guest list, row.dietary, distinctId, and proven not to fire on four ordinary error logs.

LEAK CLOSED. logViolation logged the browser-supplied document-uri verbatim; on a shared workspace that URL is /share/<token>, a bearer credential, written into the platform function log. sentry-scrub already redacted exactly that shape, so the same string was safe when thrown and unsafe when logged.

LEAK CLOSED. sendEmail logged recipient address, subject and the first 120 chars of the body whenever RESEND_API_KEY was unset. That is a configuration state, not an environment, so a production deploy that lost the key would have logged every couple's address and a slice of every wedding email. Full payload now gated on NODE_ENV development with an op-log-safe waiver; every other environment gets the recipient domain only.

9/9 pass, now wired into pnpm test (it never ran before). Includes the case 'DEFECT: a database built from the baseline lets an audit line be edited and deleted', which passes because that is the true state of a fresh database. I added the ninth case: a source-contract test that fails if audit.ts re-states the retired enforcement claim.

An unhandled production error is currently observed by nobody, and there is no alerting mechanism of any kind in either repository.

AUDIT GAP, STATED NOT CLOSED. workspace_events (line 988) is written from exactly two sites in src/server/actions/settings.ts, kinds inviteSent and inviteAccepted. Member removal, role change, share-link create/revoke, publish and account deletion are unaudited. Those writers sit in files other groups are editing concurrently this wave.
